title: Unmasking Misinformation: Leveraging CNN, BERT, and GPT Models for Robust Fake News Classification
content: In an era where misinformation and disinformation have profound impacts on public opinion, democracy, and social trust, accurately identifying and classifying false information is a critical challenge. This study explores the effectiveness of advanced machine learning models—Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), and Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPT)—for robust fake news classification. Each model brings unique strengths to the task, from CNN's ability to detect pat-terns in text to BERT and GPT’s contextual understanding of language. By comparing these models, we aim to identify optimal approaches for distinguishing truthful reporting from fabricated narratives. Our research addresses the growing need for scalable, unbiased tools capable of identifying fake news across diverse platforms and languages. With widespread accessibility, such tools could assist journalists, social media platforms, and policymakers in mitigating the rapid spread of misinformation, thereby empowering individuals with reliable, fact-based information. This work ultimately contributes to the development of more transparent and trustworthy information ecosystems, benefiting society at large.
